Genuinely hated every second of this film, either watching Salo: 120 Days Of Sodom in ages of 14-15 traumatized me so bad that I cannot enjoy Italian cinema anymore because of the flashbacks or this movie is just bad. Even though cinematography was absolutely eye catching, I can't get past the fact that it's trying to make the audience feel nostalgic for a time period that we never lived through nor give a flying fuck about. Like we did NOT live in 1945 Italy bro stop nostalgia dumping on us about a time period where literal child abuse was normalized in domestic spaces and between school teachers and students, absolutely hated the culture too, this boundary pushing, lack of etiquette disguised as comedy, putting bugs in a sleeping man's open mouth with a whole crowd laughing at his reaction there is nothing funny about this shit. If you are Georgian I think you will understand what I mean by this, it has like Georgian countryside style comedic moments that would be funny to like post soviet Georgian grandparents who miss the old times (or anybody living in these rural villages) the humor is absolutely irritating and exaggerated to the point where I literally wanted to quit around 44 minutes into the film. I heard there's a director's cut with 50 minutes of additional content and I DO NOT WANT TO SEE THAT like I'm genuinely so lucky that even though I knew nothing about this before diving into the film I didn't accidentally watch 3 hours of this dogshit cuz I would genuinely crash out. This little romance thingy with that blue eyed woman was also so stereotypical and mainstream, a completely random rule they set up for each other (standing in front of a window) to make it seem like there's something deep and romantic behind it it was genuinely disgusting. Also how Toto literally disrespects Alfredo by coming back at his hometown after Alfredo dies is the best representation of being a bad friend in media, a man tells you to stop looking back at your past and build your own life and you make an entire movie about him after he dies like such a nice friend, Salvatore, I could never thought about doing that. Overall unless you are Toto's direct classmate it's impossible to feel anything out of this movie, I never lived in China but motherfucking Yi Yi was more relatable and immersive than this it's like meant for 80 year old Italian grandpas to remember their life growing up in 90's it's genuinely so boring. Funny how The Vampire Diaries copy pasted these names, the moment I heard that Toto's girlfriend was called Elena I'm like "Salvatore and Elena? I have seen this shit before??" Overall, other than cinematography, this movie was a genuine nightmare for me to go through; again, might be a personal bias since it has the same color palette as Salo and it might be due to the flashbacks.

I posted a video on my social media asking my fellow cinemaphiles which version of Cinema Paradiso I should watch for the first time; Theatrical or Director's Cut. I kept that poll up for 3 days and nobody answered.  It became apparent to me that hardly any of my friends have actually seen it, or those that have simply didn't have the time nor interest in giving their opinion. I ended up watching the Theatrical version and I'm really glad I did...because I don't think I'd have had the patience for an extra hour of this. I remember for years being encouraged as a movie lover to see this film, and now after finally watching it, I found it to be completely dull, long, and tiresome. It has its visuals, sure, but the story overall just didn't keep me enthralled. One and done.

Obra completamente datada por apresentar uma história simples, que é carregada mais pela amizade entre Toto e Alfredo que pelo enredo em si. The best thing here is how badly everyone behaves at the cinema. They talk back, interrupt and pursue interests of their own while the film happens in front of them. A screening has to compete with the people attending it. Tornatore is good at keeping those little disturbances alive around the same attraction, and I like the place most when it seems impossible to manage. The priest ringing his bell at every kiss belongs to that world. Alfredo has to do the actual cutting, which gives censorship the absurdity of an additional chore for a man who already has a machine to operate. When the projection reaches the square, the pleasure is immediate: the film has found more people, and the building can no longer contain the occasion. These passages have a sociability that the later nostalgia struggles to recover. As Salvatore gets older, the past becomes suspiciously well prepared for remembrance. The romance has less particularity than the cinema, and Alfredo increasingly speaks in advice that sounds ready to accompany somebody else's flashback. Noiret brings warmth and fatigue to it, but he is being made to organise the meaning of a life while still living in it. Salvatore's departure and return give the film a tidiness that the early scenes hadn't needed. The reel of discarded kisses is a lovely idea. It lets Alfredo express something through the work of his hands, using material that a small authority decided nobody should see. I can feel the generosity of that gesture. The swelling score and repeated attention to Salvatore's reaction make the emotion harder for me to inhabit, though; every instant seems to have an assigned degree of poignancy. What had been a crowded, unruly pleasure ends up carefully arranged for one man's tears. I missed the people who used to shout at the screen.

There are many “love letter to movies” movies, and Cinema Paradiso is the one of the 80s. This grounded slice-of-life movie tells the story of Toto in Giancaldo, Sicily at three different points in his lifetime: childhood, teenagehood, and adulthood. Each of these points serve as the different “acts” of the movie. Act one displays Toto’s introduction to the projection room and falling in love with film. When I was a similar age, I fell in love with movies and watched a lot of what was considered “nerdy”, like Star Trek, Lord of the Rings, and especially Indiana Jones. Something I especially loved doing was watching the behind the scenes of these movies on DVD, similar to how Toto learned how to use the projection camera from Alfredo. As act two transitions into Toto as a teenager, Alfredo convinces him to leave and find himself outside of Giancaldo. I find this similar to my own experience of convincing my parents to let me live on campus and be away from them so I can finally have independence. While Cinema Paradiso is definitely put together incredibly well, I found the pacing too slow for my tastes, and I wouldn’t necessarily choose to watch it on my own. I’d rate it similar to Casablanca, as they’re both older movies I appreciate for the craftsmanship, but I can’t find anything that especially stands out to me. Definitely watch it if you’re serious about movies, but this isn’t a movie for casual viewers.

有中文 Beyond its homage to cinema and nostalgia, “paradise” also carries a self-reflexive dimension. Both stem from our fear that life cannot last forever, as well as our desire to imagine something beautiful beyond the limits of reality. This is very much how Tornatore approaches the film, using a nostalgic filter to soften the wounds of war, social divisions, and personal struggles. But what do the cinema and cinema itself actually mean? Why does the protagonist become a director? What does filmmaking mean as part of reality itself? These questions seem largely overlooked. The first half still offers a fairly complete sense of what cinema means, but in the second half, cinema ultimately becomes little more than a blunt, incomplete symbol of time and emotion, folded into a rather conventional melodrama. The audiovisual style also rarely goes beyond effective emotional manipulation. I particularly dislike the score when it lacks restraint, feeling painfully contrived. It merely keeps reaffirming the same emotional register, flattening the film's two halves into a single, uniform mood. Giuseppe Tornatore’s Cinema Paradiso is the quintessential filmmaker's paradox. It is a film with such a poignant and compelling message about the vitality and importance of art, yet it is conveyed in the exact antithesis of this very ideology. It is an overly schmaltzy, painfully idealistic portrait of cinema, feeling like gimmicky nostalgia bait designed to generate waterworks from audience members rather than to offer any sort of meaning or value to art and the beauty of cinema itself. This makes it feel quite shallow underneath its excessive dramatism. While this is by no means a train wreck of a film and features several outstanding elements, it is still difficult to reject its flaws. Firstly, there is that excellent score from the legendary Ennio Morricone (albeit purposely engineered to be overtly sentimental). Additionally, while the cinematography is by no means a masterpiece, there are some genuinely phenomenal wide long shots of the gorgeous, quaint Italian countryside and some excellent uses of light throughout, making it rather pleasant to look at. However, unfortunately, that is where my praise for this film ends. I just find this film to be the embodiment of antithesis, as its artistic message and ethics don’t align with the film's execution and manufacture. The film relies way too heavily on this overly manipulative, straightforward, and highly unoriginal plot, relying heavily on traditional Italian and film stereotypes: the strict mother, Maria; the young, hopeful, love-stricken protagonist, Salvatore; as well as the wise, elderly mentor, Alfredo. Whether it be through the various caricatures, its black-and-white portrayal of morality, or its rather stereotypical portrayals of 20th-century, war-ridden Italy—as well as its hyper-predictable plot evident in scenes like the fire of the original Cinema Paradiso, where Toto magically saves Alfredo’s life, or Salvatore's cliché, heartbroken love life and brief experience in the war (something evident in films and mediums long before this)—the plot of this film feels repetitive and redundant. Unfortunately, this film for me feels like a gimmick. It feels like a hoax to fabricate tears and emotions from the general public without relying on any truly artistic or profound message justifying its use and love of art. While Cinema Paradiso is absolutely a successful love letter to cinema, as it hits all the hallmarks of a classic touching film designed to please the masses, which I can respect, I just find it lacks a reason justifying its profound respect for cinema itself. It operates in a way which subverts the film's entire morals. It’s a paradox that a film so dedicated to the uniqueness and beauty of cinema is delivered in one of the most conventional, overly melodramatic, and standard portrayals of film put to screen, making this film feel like such a disappointment to genuine art. Rather than exploring profound questions on life, creativity, identity, or the true craftsmanship and emotional and honest intensity of auteur filmmaking, the film harks back to nostalgic and relatable messages, making its overall tone feel shallow. Overall, Cinema Paradiso is by no means a bad film. While I don’t hate it at all, I strongly dislike what it represents. While, yes, it’s tongue-in-cheek, a little cheesy in moments, and fails to be a true artistic statement by falling into several conventions and stereotypes, it is still excellently scored and serves as a nice love letter to cinema for those who appreciate its sentimental tone. And while the ending is undoubtedly cheesy, it’s still incredibly effective and a beautiful homage to classic films (probably my favorite aspect of the film). While I do absolutely love the original sentiment, it’s just been executed so poorly and so bizarrely. The film just unfortunately disappoints me and, in my opinion, serves as probably one of the biggest paradoxes in the entire history of cinema: a film that cares more about pulling the heartstrings of the audience than actually caring about art and film itself.

i understand why cinema paradiso is so beloved, and i can absolutely see what tornatore is trying to do with it. the cinema becoming the heart of this little village, totò growing up surrounded by films, alfredo becoming this father figure, and eventually leaving everything behind to become a filmmaker : there’s something really beautiful about the whole idea of cinema as both a home and something you eventually have to leave behind. but somehow, i remained completely detached from it. i usually love films about nostalgia, memory, lost time and the lives we could have lived, but here the sentimentality felt a little too obvious for me. i could see the emotion in almost every scene without actually feeling it myself. even the final montage, which i understand is supposed to be devastating, left me more appreciative than moved. and honestly, i think the extended version made this even harder for me. i actually liked the idea behind alfredo pushing totò away from his old life, but i could have done without the adult reunion with elena. there was something much more poignant to me about her simply remaining a lost love, something that belonged to a life totò could no longer get back. bringing her back decades later made the story feel more melodramatic when i would have preferred the absence to remain absolute. i can appreciate what the film is trying to say about memory, cinema and letting go, but it never became as emotionally powerful for me as it clearly is for so many people.

De verdad que pocas películas me han hecho estar tan feliz, tan triste y tener tantas emociones en una sola película. No sabía casi nada de la película y lo que me he encontrado ha sido una maravilla. De verdad que no tengo cómo describir todo lo que he sentido viendo esta película. De verdad que ha sido una experiencia maravillosa. La historia de Toto y sobre todo Alfredo juntos me parece una de las mejores y más bonitas historias que he visto nunca. Creo que sabe mezclar genial todo, el humor, porque hacen muchas bromas en la película, los momentos serios, los duros y, sobre todo, los emotivos. Esta película, mira que pocas lo hacen, diría que casi ninguna me ha hecho tener los ojos llorosos tanto como esta. Alfredo me ha parecido uno de los mejores personajes que he visto en toda la historia del cine. No tanto por cómo actúa ni qué es lo que hace dentro de la peli, sino por el cariño que le coges. De verdad que pocas muertes me han dejado así de mal y de verdad que lo quiero con locura y por él recordaré esta película toda mi vida. En esta peli te muestran tus propias emociones viendo la propia película reflejadas en todo aquello el cual va al cinema Paradiso. Y otras cosas que me han fascinado y me han encantado de la película son todos los personajes de fondo. Cada uno tiene su propia historia o, por lo menos, su propia personalidad, los cuales les llegas también a coger cariños, como es el cura, el que construye y ayuda a Totoro en el cine, incluso el propio loco de dentro de la plaza. Y esa escena, la escena del incendio. Pocas escenas en el cine te pueden dejar con tanta angustia y tan malestar como es esa. De un momento tan bonito y precioso que es tan llegar a eso. De verdad que es totalmente desgarrador y puede ser una de las mejores escenas de la historia del cine. No sé por qué coño no me vi esta película hace ya años, pero de verdad que la disfruto como un niño pequeño. He sido el propio Toto viendo sus películas en el cine. Me he sentido igual que él. Y por no hablar de la fotografía y todas las referencias que hay en la película sobre otras películas. Eso me pareció fascinante. Creo que hay planos que son hermosos dentro de la película, los cuales te muestran todo lo que sienten todos los personajes. De verdad, las películas de el 70 al 90 de Italia, de verdad, que son una joya todas. Una puta obra de arte.

Um filme que demonstra perfeitamente que muitas vezes podemos deixar um sítio, mas esse sítio nunca nos deixa a nós. A relação entre Salvatore e Alfredo é bonita, genuína e sincera. Uma ligação que me cativou imenso e que acaba por ser um dos grandes pilares emocionais do filme. É uma história sobre crescer, partir, recordar e perceber que, por mais longe que a vida nos leve, há sempre partes da nossa infância que permanecem connosco. A nostalgia está presente em cada momento, mas nunca de uma forma vazia. Faz-nos recordar pessoas, lugares e momentos que, por vezes, só percebemos verdadeiramente quando já ficaram para trás. E depois há a banda sonora de Ennio Morricone, absolutamente extraordinária, que torna tudo ainda mais especial. Um filme sobre a vida, as memórias e o amor pelo cinema. Daqueles que nos fazem sentir que acabámos de assistir a algo verdadeiramente especial. Filme perfeito.

Estranhamente, a primeira vez que ouvi falar de Cinema Paradiso foi em uma aula de biologia. Era 2014, eu tinha 14 anos e meu professor também era padre. Uma combinação que, na minha cabeça, precisava de algumas explicações. A gente sempre conversava sobre filmes. E eu lembro como se fosse hoje de ele dizer que ficava abismado com a minha paixão pelo cinema, que achava aquilo incrível. Numa época em que, pra muita gente ao meu redor, assistir a um filme era só uma forma de passar o tempo, acho que me marcou alguém perceber o quanto aquilo significava pra mim. Talvez eu mesmo ainda não soubesse explicar. Foi numa dessas conversas que ele me recomendou um filme italiano antigo chamado Cinema Paradiso . Não assisti. Eu já via filmes antigos, mas um drama italiano de mais de duas horas reunia fatores demais contra a disposição do meu eu de 14 anos. Deixei pra depois, como a gente faz com tanta coisa, sem pensar muito no tamanho que esse depois pode ter. Só tive aulas com ele naquele primeiro ano. Algum tempo depois, ele faleceu. A recomendação ficou. Acho curioso como algumas pessoas continuam participando da nossa vida sem saber. Como uma conversa qualquer pode ficar guardada por doze anos, esperando que a gente finalmente chegue até ela. Escolhi Cinema Paradiso como meu filme de número 2000 no Letterboxd. Sei que é uma conta meio imaginária. Existem filmes que nunca marquei, outros que vi e já não lembro. Se contasse as vezes que reassisti cada um, talvez fossem quatro ou cinco mil, porque sabe-se lá quantas vezes os filmes dos X-Men ou Premonição passaram no repeat lá em casa. Mas gosto de marcar algumas coisas que considero importantes. Mesmo sabendo que o número é impreciso, o que me trouxe até ele existe. Assim como Totò, minha relação com o cinema começou muito cedo. Algumas ausências fizeram parte disso. Não sei até onde consigo separar as coisas, nem se preciso, mas acho que havia muito espaço pra encontrar naqueles filmes uma companhia. E havia também aquela vontade de viver o que eu via. Eu fui crescendo e imaginando que, em algum momento, a vida teria um pouco daquilo. Lembro da primeira vez que assisti a Halloween . Era uma quarta-feira depois do almoço. Sexta-feira 13 foi num sábado de manhã. Clube da Luta , num fim de tarde de sábado. Brilho Eterno de uma Mente sem Lembranças , numa quinta-feira à noite. Não sei por que lembro com tanta precisão dessas coisas. Penso em quantos dias inteiros desapareceram da minha memória, enquanto uma tarde em que sentei pra assistir a um filme continua aqui. E lembro das pessoas. De quem escolheu passar aquele tempo comigo. Se eu tivesse assistido sozinho, seria outra experiência. Com outra pessoa, também. E, cara, se fosse com a mesma pessoa em outro dia, já seria diferente. Às vezes penso nisso quando reassisto a alguma coisa. O filme continua lá, mas aquela sessão, com aquelas pessoas, naquele momento da nossa vida, não tem como repetir. Sou grato por termos dividido isso. Mesmo quando foi só mais um filme num dia qualquer. Sempre admirei o cinema e, ao mesmo tempo, acho que esperei demais da vida por causa dele. Ainda espero, talvez. Algumas histórias parecem tão possíveis enquanto a gente está assistindo. Você pensa que um dia vai viver alguma coisa assim, que certas conversas poderiam ser mais bonitas, que algumas despedidas poderiam fazer mais sentido. Que a vida podia ser um pouco menos crua em determinados momentos. Mas, se tudo fosse como nos filmes, será que assistir a eles teria a mesma importância? Talvez eu não procurasse tanto uma coisa que já estivesse vivendo. Ao mesmo tempo, o cinema consegue fazer uma tarde qualquer, uma conversa ou alguém olhando pela janela parecerem suficientes. E eu fico pensando em quantas coisas da minha vida pareceriam bonitas numa tela, mas passaram por mim sem que eu percebesse, porque eu estava esperando alguma outra coisa acontecer. Alfredo conta a Totò a história de um soldado que aceita esperar cem dias pela mulher que ama e vai embora na última noite, antes de completar a espera. Não sei como Totò entendeu aquela história. Não sei se eu teria entendido da mesma forma aos 14 anos. Talvez daqui a alguns anos eu veja tudo isso de outro jeito. Mas hoje fiquei pensando se assistir a um filme não é um pouco como ficar diante daquela janela. Você se senta num lugar escuro, em silêncio, e vê as coisas acontecendo. Passam quarenta, cinquenta, sessenta dias. Você espera, deseja, acredita na possibilidade de alguma coisa. E, por mais perto que chegue, vai embora no nonagésimo nono. Talvez eu esteja viajando nessa comparação. Mas penso que o centésimo dia seria alguma forma de alcançar aquilo. De finalmente viver o que, até então, só foi possível olhar. E um final, por mais bonito que seja, não consegue fazer isso pela gente. A música aumenta, os créditos sobem, a luz acende e os olhos ficam ofuscados. Você ainda está sentindo tudo aquilo, mas precisa levantar, procurar suas coisas, decidir o que vai comer. Acho que já saí de muitos filmes querendo ficar mais um pouco. E não sei se queria que a história continuasse ou se queria continuar sendo a pessoa que eu era enquanto assistia. Aquela que, por duas horas, acreditou em certas coisas com uma facilidade que fora dali nem sempre consegue. Hoje cheguei ao filme que meu professor me indicou. Fico pensando no que ele reconheceu naquele menino de 14 anos, no que imaginou que eu encontraria aqui. Queria poder conversar com ele sobre isso. Contar que assisti, que lembrei, que passei todos esses anos vendo filmes e ainda tenho dificuldade de explicar o tamanho que isso tem pra mim. Talvez, aos 14, eu estivesse esperando que o cinema me mostrasse a vida que ainda ia viver. Hoje olho pra esses filmes e encontro tanto da vida que já passou. As pessoas, as casas, as tardes que pareciam não ter nada demais. E fico pensando se, enquanto eu esperava que a minha vida se parecesse com um filme, era isso que estava acontecendo. Se aquele dia qualquer que eu mal percebi enquanto vivia é justamente o que, agora, eu passaria duas horas no escuro pra ver outra vez.
